# High-loop proposal experiments for exact parametric-IBP closure

Date: 2026-08-31

Status: bounded Stage 1 research plan, not an implementation or closure result

## Scope and authority boundary

This note freezes five falsifiable experiments for the complete authenticated four-, five-, and
six-loop single-scale vacuum manifests, with scalar-product counts `K = 10`, `K = 15`, and
`K = 21`. Every experiment starts with the canonical `K = 6` control as an ungated semantic and
instrumentation calibration. Its first promotion decision is the stated `K = 10` gate; only a pass
there permits `K = 15`, whose pass in turn permits `K = 21`.

Here `K` is family arity, not a topology count or a complete-graph label: a vacuum family with
`L` independent loop momenta has `K = L(L+1)/2` independent scalar-product coordinates. Thus
`K = 6`, `10`, `15`, and `21` label the common arities of the three-, four-, five-, and six-loop
pressure manifests. From four loops onward each complete manifest is multi-parent: the edge sets
of graphs `K_4`, `K_5`, `K_6`, and `K_7` describe only the canonical root-coordinate proxies, not
universal parent families. In particular, graph `K_{3,3}` is already not a restriction of the
four-loop `K_5` proxy under a unimodular routing. This numeric arity `K`, a graph label `K_r`, and
the coefficient field customarily written `\mathbb K(n)` are three unrelated uses of the letter.

The experiments may improve discovery proposals or measure scaling. They do **not** authorize:

- a four-, five-, or six-loop artifact, terminal, owner, or closure claim;
- Stage 2 tensor work, high-loop production scheduling, distributed-memory infrastructure, GPU
  integration, or a public API, artifact-schema, or Cargo change;
- replacing native-target-zero inverse incidence, exact selected-support lift, full regenerated-
  source replay, guard and descent admission, or bottom-up immutable lower-owner coverage;
- treating a symbolic rule, cut system, quotient dimension, modular no-hit, stable cross-probe
  pattern, or exhausted proposal source as evidence of exact nonexistence; or
- requiring or installing a minimal master basis. A temporary quotient-monomial basis in one
  gated algebra experiment is computational scratch state, not a semantic terminal catalog.

All proposal state remains task-, epoch-, and probe-local. `SampledDeclaredModuleDual` keeps its
existing narrow fixed-sample authority, guarded strata keep failing closed, and cross-probe unions
remain telemetry only. A proposed hit becomes meaningful only after the existing exact and
semantic admission path accepts it.

## Architectural priority

The recommended execution order is **experiment 1, then 4, then 5, then 2, then 3**.

| Priority | Experiment | Candidate | RustRed role | Reason for placement |
| ---: | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 1 | Gram-minor/syzygy reuse | propose exact ordinary-source requests | best fit to target-zero exact replay and family-local caching |
| 2 | 4 | block-dual batching and hit slicing | reduce epochs and exact support | native extension of the current certificate-driven campaign |
| 3 | 5 | independent multipoint lanes and blocking | improve bounded modular throughput | preserves per-probe evidence if lanes never share authority |
| 4 | 2 | seedless/symbolic lowering rules | propose guarded exact circuits | high upside, but bulk/boundary coverage is unproved at high loop order |
| 5 | 3 | finite quotient/action matrices | propose relations after stable modular quotient preflight | highest algebraic and positive-dimensional failure risk |

No reviewed primary source supplies RustRed's combined guarantees of a nonminimal finite terminal
set, exact ordinary-source provenance, guarded chart coverage, immutable lower-owner discharge,
and terminal closure. RustRed therefore remains the verifier rather than adopting another method's
completeness claim.

## Primary-source basis

- Böhm et al. give an explicit complete generating set of dimension-preserving Baikov logarithmic
  vector fields for any loop and external-momentum count, obtained from Gram-determinant Laplace
  expansions and submaximal minors:
  [arXiv:1712.09737](https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.09737).
- NeatIBP 1.1 combines syzygy simplification, spanning cuts, and Kira integration, but its generated
  or cut systems remain proposal inputs here:
  [arXiv:2502.20778](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.20778).
- Smith and Zeng construct syzygy-constrained symbolic rules and test rank-20 double-box and
  pentabox integrals:
  [arXiv:2507.11140](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.11140). De la Cruz and Kosower construct
  generic-index lowering operators without a finite seed region:
  [arXiv:2602.22111](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22111). Feng et al. iteratively generate and test
  sectorwise generating-function rules on an index lattice:
  [arXiv:2605.09541](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09541).
- Kira 3 demonstrates that post-forward-elimination dependency selection can sharply reduce
  equation count, memory, and finite-field solve time:
  [arXiv:2505.20197](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.20197). Blade supplies a complementary
  block-triangular decomposition programme:
  [arXiv:2405.14621](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.14621).
- Companion tensor algebra casts quotient-ring division and intersection calculations as matrix
  operations, but the published pipeline projects onto a chosen cohomology/master basis:
  [arXiv:2408.16668](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.16668). The Macaulay-matrix predecessor derives
  finite quotient actions and recurrence relations:
  [arXiv:2204.12983](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.12983). Lee and Pomeransky relate isolated critical
  points to finite integral-space dimension:
  [arXiv:1308.6676](https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.6676).
- Crisanti et al. associate magic relations with higher-dimensional critical varieties and give a
  practical warning against assuming an isolated finite quotient:
  [arXiv:2605.29789](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.29789).
- Smirnov and Zeng report simultaneous finite-field probes and sparse balanced reconstruction:
  [arXiv:2409.19099](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.19099). FIRE 7 reports multiprime modular
  benchmarks:
  [arXiv:2510.07150](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.07150). Linton et al. give a two-dimensional
  row/column block structure for parallel finite-field elimination while avoiding known-zero
  transformation blocks:
  [arXiv:1806.04211](https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.04211).

Published claims above motivate the experiments; none of the papers establishes `K = 10`,
`K = 15`, or `K = 21` closure for RustRed's equal-mass vacuum manifests.

## Common protocol and measurements

Each comparison uses the same authenticated family, decorated sector, target-zero request,
immutable lower-owner snapshot, resource policy, prime/sample schedule, and deterministic ordering.
It records both aggregate results and every timeout, resource rejection, guarded stratum, censored
family, and unresolved member. A method may advance from `K = 10` to `K = 15`, and then to
`K = 21`, only if it passes its gate at the preceding size.

The common measurements are:

- unique translated requests `N_req`, retained independent rows `R`, projected columns `C`, input
  nonzeros `Z`, and peak elimination fill `F`;
- epochs, inverse-incidence visits, fully evaluated candidates, and modular rank gained per retained
  row;
- selected exact support, maximum exact coefficient bit length, exact-lift time, and full-replay
  time;
- symbolic generator/rule count, maximum degree, guard or wall count, and scratch expression size
  where applicable;
- wall time, peak resident memory, admitted owners per CPU-hour, and the fraction of declared tasks
  reaching each proved evidence state; and
- adjacent scaling exponents `p_X(a,b) = log(X_b^+ / X_a^+) / log(b / a)` for
  `(a,b) = (10,15)` and `(15,21)`, where discrete counts use `X^+ = max(1,X)` and intrinsically
  positive wall-time and resident-memory measurements use their measured values.

Universal kill conditions are any accepted relation that fails exact replay, any lost guard or
lower-owner obligation, nondeterministic evidence under a thread-count change, a proposal-derived
no-relation claim, an omitted manifest member, or resource use beyond the preregistered envelope.

## Experiment 1: hash-consed Gram-minor syzygy proposer

**Hypothesis.** Family- and sector-scoped hash-consing of Gram entries, Laplace expansions, and
submaximal minors can cheaply propose useful ordinary-source combinations across related tasks.
Cache keys include the exact family, sector, variable map, coefficient context, and decoration;
symmetry or graph similarity alone never aliases entries. Every proposal must resolve to original
ordinary-source instances before exact lift.

**Comparison and metrics.** Compare the current inverse-incidence campaign with a proposal lane
using specialized logarithmic syzygies. In addition to the common metrics, record DAG nodes versus
naive expression nodes, cache-hit and specialization ratios, generator degree, and provenance-
resolution failures.

**Gate.** At `K = 10`, require at least a `1.5x` median improvement in wall time or peak memory and
`100%` exact ordinary-source replay for accepted candidates. After measuring `K = 15` or `K = 21`,
apply the same local improvement gate and allow no worsening larger than `0.25` in the corresponding
adjacent scaling exponent. Kill the lane if expression swell erases reuse, a cache identity crosses
a family/context boundary, or a proposal cannot recover exact provenance.

## Experiment 2: generic-index lowering-rule proposer

**Hypothesis.** Syzygy-constrained, seedless, or fixed-direction generating-function operators can
amortize discovery across many targets without installing a master basis. Compile bulk and
boundary rules separately against the current partition and immutable lower-owner snapshot.
Applicability walls become explicit guards; a compiled rule only nominates an exact circuit.

**Comparison and metrics.** Test syzygy/seedless and generating-function backends separately.
Record symbolic system rows, columns, and nonzeros; operator count and degree; coefficient height;
guard/wall count; build time and memory; exact-admitted target coverage; and amortized cost
`build + applications` against ordinary discovery for the same targets.

**Gate.** At `K = 10`, require replayable proposals for at least `80%` of declared target tasks and
lower total amortized cost after 20 targets. At `K = 15` and `K = 21`, the same coverage and cost
gate applies. For rule count, maximum degree, maximum coefficient bit height, and guard count, use
the `max(1,X)` convention above and require every adjacent exponent to be at most `4`; record the
corresponding ordinary-discovery value beside it rather than hiding a worse baseline. An uncovered
wall or failed implication is a proposal miss, never evidence of absence.

## Experiment 3: zero-dimensional quotient/action-matrix oracle

**Hypothesis.** In sectors whose saturated critical ideal has stable modular evidence consistent
with zero dimension, quotient reduction may propose compact target relations more cheaply than
translated-row discovery.

**Preflight.** Compute Krull dimension, Hilbert function, and monomial staircase over three
deterministic primes and require agreement; use a fourth prime as held-out verification. Construct
action matrices only after a stable modular zero-dimensional result. This is not a characteristic-
zero dimension or Gröbner certificate; only the resulting relation's ordinary-source provenance
and exact replay can admit a proposal. Positive-dimensional, inconsistent, or resource-exhausted
preflights return typed fallback to ordinary inverse incidence.

**Comparison and metrics.** Record quotient dimension `mu`, Gröbner/Macaulay rows and nonzeros,
action-matrix density, fill and memory, staircase stability, proposed support, time relative to the
current campaign, and exact-replay rate.

**Gate.** At least half of the declared sectors at each `K` must pass preflight, and replayable
candidates must use less than half the corresponding inverse-incidence wall time and peak memory.
Compare `mu` against the baseline projected column count `C`, action-matrix nonzeros against
baseline `Z`, action-matrix fill against baseline `F`, and peak memory against baseline resident
memory. Kill or fall back if a candidate exponent exceeds its paired baseline exponent by more than
`0.25`, if critical varieties are positive-dimensional, if staircases vary by prime, or if any
candidate fails exact replay. Neither modular quotient dimension nor an empty quotient query has
closure authority.

## Experiment 4: block-dual batching and post-hit dependency slicing

**Hypothesis.** A small deterministic block of independent right obstructions can nominate a
higher-rank-gain row batch per fresh epoch, while provenance slicing can reduce the exact minor
after a hit.

**Comparison and metrics.** Use a `2 x 2` comparison: one obstruction versus up to four normalized
independent obstructions, and current exact support versus a backward dependency slice. Enumerate
inverse incidence once over the union of obstruction supports, rank candidates by residual-
signature rank, and add them in stable order. Slicing is permitted only after a modular hit; the
complete materialized rows and empty-residual census remain untouched for sampled-dual admission.
Record epochs-to-hit, visits, evaluated rows, rank gain, `R/Z/F`, exact-support ratio, coefficient
height, and lift/replay time and memory.

**Gate.** Require at least `2x` fewer epochs or exact-lift nonzeros, no more than `25%` additional
modular work, identical admitted outcomes, and deterministic results at each `K`. Kill block
batching if it only front-loads rows, and reject any slicing path that could prune a no-hit census.

## Experiment 5: independent multipoint lanes and deterministic blocking

**Hypothesis.** Probe states with an identical raw-request fingerprint can share immutable sparse
structure and coefficient evaluation while retaining independent values, reducers, obstructions,
evidence, and budgets. Deterministic row/column blocks may improve locality without changing the
global pivot order.

**Comparison and metrics.** Benchmark lane widths `1`, `4`, `8`, and `16`; split a group as soon as
campaign request fingerprints diverge. Compare the current sparse layout with fixed two-dimensional
blocking that omits known-zero transformation blocks. Record terms and probes per second, lane
efficiency, first divergence epoch, synchronization cost, fill, aggregate and per-probe memory, and
byte-identical per-probe outcomes across thread counts.

**Gate.** At width `8`, require at least `3x` probe throughput, aggregate peak memory no greater
than `2x` one lane, and identical independent outcomes at each `K`. If campaigns normally diverge
after their first augmentation or blocking increases fill enough to remove the gain, retain only
shared immutable coefficient evaluation. During Stage 1 this remains a bounded in-process
benchmark; it does not authorize a production high-loop scheduler, accelerator backend, or
distributed execution layer.

## Promotion record

### K6 control calibration

The first generic scheduler calibration has now been recorded on the six
full-rank orbit representatives of the three-loop `K = 6` pressure family at
three independent primes. All 18 first epochs have 90 rows, 253 columns, and
918 structural entries. The target-augmented rank equals the forbidden rank
(90) throughout, so there is no bootstrap hit. Exact residual pairing
nominates between 3,586 and 3,822 nonzero translated-source requests before an
explicit one-epoch stop. This validates deterministic accounting, probe
isolation, terminal-owner partitioning, and the need for proposal compression;
it does not measure or promote any of experiments 1--5 and cannot be
extrapolated into a `K = 10`, `K = 15`, or `K = 21` scaling result.

The one-epoch infrastructure limitation has since been removed without
promoting an experiment. Each probe now owns a transactional growing epoch
sequence: a successful request set must strictly contain its predecessor, a
fresh physical plan and exact maximal stratum are rebuilt, and the new domain
is authenticated against the immediately preceding domain before the epoch is
committed. A separate sealed bridge can losslessly lower a replayed exact
circuit into a resource-admitted `ParametricRule` and direct
`SourceViewBatch`, using compact source-owned shift buffers and an independent
full-physical-column replay. This bridge deliberately cannot construct a
`RuleCell`, owner, terminal, or closure artifact. These changes remove the
common multi-epoch and exact-lowering blockers shared by experiments 1--4 and
make future exact hits reusable by the existing foundry. Their
experiment-specific Gram/syzygy, generating-function/seedless, quotient, and
block-dual proposal compilers remain unimplemented. The infrastructure does
not improve the unfavorable first-epoch K6 census and is not scaling evidence.

No experiment is currently promoted. A future result must append the exact manifest revision,
resource envelope, raw aggregate table, all censored members, adjacent scaling exponents, and the
strongest proved evidence state. A favorable benchmark may justify a separate implementation
proposal; it cannot by itself widen Stage 1 or authorize an artifact.

### Bounded residual-frontier control

A non-promoted scheduler control now separates exhaustive residual authority
from frame-growth policy. Only nonzero residual rows are scored, using exact
prospective forbidden/allowed classification, obstruction-support overlap,
row width, and canonical identity; at most 32 are retained per epoch. The
eight-epoch first-sector K6 run grows from 90 to 314 rows and from 253 to 413
columns, ending with equal forbidden/augmented ranks of 279/279. It scans
63,573 candidate rows and 645,012 exact source terms without finding a hit.

This is useful negative evidence. Bounded ranking prevents one obstruction
from adding thousands of rows to the next frame, but a scalar score ignores
batch-shared columns and linear independence across the obstruction space.
The next control must therefore select against an independent obstruction
block, reuse previously evaluated rows, and report marginal block-rank gain.
No part of this result promotes experiments 1--5 or constitutes K6 closure.
